dedupe_keys.name: analysis of wind induced interference effects on a realistic low rise building in an urban area

description: Analysis of wind-induced interference effects on a realistic low-rise building in an urban area is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Catherine Gorle, Stanford University (stanford.edu). This project has investigated the pressure loads on a realistic low-rise building configuration within an urban area in order to study wind-induced pressure loads due to the surrounding buildings. The test case is the Y2E2 building in Stanford Engineering Quad. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Wind hazards,  wind loading, low-rise building, interference effects. Published 2024-10-17. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
